elements.problem: The page lists a cluster of signs (thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60) that together make dehydration likely. The rule ORs them, so any single item is enough: thirst alone, dry mouth alone, or diastolic < 60 alone makes dehydration 'probable' and, through active_condition Dehydration, makes the patient Urgent. It should use and, or at least any2. BP < 90/60 is also split into systolic < 90 OR diastolic < 60, which is a defensible reading but makes an isolated diastolic of 58 enough on its own.

rule_level_problems.problem: OR over a sign cluster: any single sign (e.g. thirst or dry mouth) gives probable dehydration, and via active_condition Dehydration the patient becomes Urgent. The page means the combination. Use and, or any2.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: weakness or tiredness with red-box findings
rule_level_problems.problem: (active_condition (snomed_concept "Heart failure" "disorder")) is satisfied by any known, stable heart failure diagnosis, not only the page's 'orthopnoea + leg swelling, heart failure likely'. A tired patient with chronic HF is always made Urgent. The same applies to (active_condition Fever) with no 3-day bound.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: weakness or tiredness with red-box findings
rule_level_problems.problem: The 'Temperature ≥ 38°C … in past 3 days' arm has no onset window; (< (onset (active_condition Fever)) (time_ago 3 days)) is expressible and was not used.

'Difficulty talking' has no SNOMED descendants, so speech findings recorded as Dysarthria, Aphasia or Slurred speech do not trigger the stroke/TIA or Urgent rules. Limb/face findings only match when both the Sudden onset and Asymmetry qualifiers are recorded.

summary: The most consequential problem is that probable dehydration fires on any one of thirst, dry mouth, poor turgor or low BP. Because the Urgent rule references it, a tired patient with thirst alone becomes Urgent. Urgent also fires on any known heart failure via active_condition, and 'fever in past 3 days' has no time bound. Otherwise the red box is fully and correctly encoded (stroke/TIA possible, glucose thresholds, chest pain, breathing, worsening leg weakness, HF probable), with Hb < 6 correctly left out as not representable.
